violations.where: Data model → Credit Note: `credit_note_number` "own `CN-` sequence, strictly sequential; kept separate from `invoice_number`"; R-d11; S31
violations.why: The Sheet decision d:credit_note_numbering states credit notes "share the invoice number sequence." The spec does the exact opposite — a separate CN- sequence — silently reversing the decision it cites.
violations.fix_hint: Either update the Sheet decision to a separate sequence, or number credit notes within the invoice sequence as the Sheet dictates.

violations.where: Invoice lifecycle lists 7 states incl. `viewed`; Data model Invoice `status` enum = (draft,sent,partially_paid,paid,overdue,void) with no `viewed`
violations.why: The lifecycle section adds a `viewed` state and sent→viewed transition, but the Invoice status enum and status-derivation in the data model have no `viewed` state at all. The two sections disagree about the set of legal Invoice states.
violations.fix_hint: Reconcile: either add `viewed` to the enum/derivation or remove the `viewed` state from the lifecycle.

violations.where: Invoice lifecycle row `sent`→`viewed` | Who: Client | "Client receives and opens the invoice" vs permissions Client column all ✗ and note 2 "performs no in-app action" and non-goals "no email open-tracking or 'viewed' signal"
violations.why: The lifecycle has the Client (an actor with no account and no in-app action) drive a state transition, and relies on an open/viewed signal the permissions prose and non-goals both say does not exist. The scenario the lifecycle describes is forbidden by the permission matrix and explicitly denied elsewhere.
violations.fix_hint: Remove the Client-driven `viewed` transition; there is no viewed signal or Client action in v1.

violations.where: Invoice status derivation + R-r3 balance cap (amount − payments − credits) + R-r7 (paid iff payments==amount)
violations.why: With any credit note applied, R-r3 caps recordable payments at amount−credits, so payments can never equal amount, so R-r7's `paid` is unreachable. Meanwhile status derivation only defines sent (requires credited_amount==0), partially_paid (requires amount_paid>0), and paid (amount_paid==amount). A credited invoice with amount_paid=0 (e.g. $450 invoice, $200 credit) matches NO status and can never leave it — an unsatisfiable, statusless stuck record.
violations.fix_hint: Add an explicit 'settled/closed-by-credit' status and make status derivation exhaustive for any credited invoice.

violations.where: Permissions matrix "Review a Statement | Bookkeeper ✓" vs Statement lifecycle `generated`→`reviewed` | Who: Firm Owner only (⟨a8⟩)
violations.why: The matrix grants the Bookkeeper the ability to review a Statement, but the Statement lifecycle allows only the Firm Owner to perform the review transition. The two sections disagree about who can review; the Sheet action a8 is Firm-Owner-only.
violations.fix_hint: Deny Bookkeeper review in the matrix or add a Bookkeeper review transition — but a8 restricts review to the Firm Owner.

violations.where: R-r5 / permissions note 1 / Delegation entity — Bookkeeper with delegation may void
violations.why: Sheet r5 states "Only the Firm Owner may void an invoice." The spec weakens this by granting a delegated Bookkeeper void rights. The Sheet's own x7 conflicts with r5's "only," and the spec resolves toward x7, contradicting the literal inviolable rule.
violations.fix_hint: Reconcile r5 and x7 at the Sheet level before implementing delegated void.

violations.where: R-r6 / permissions note 1 — Bookkeeper with delegation may change monthly rate
violations.why: Sheet r6 states "Only the Firm Owner may change a client's monthly rate," but the spec permits a delegated Bookkeeper to do so, weakening the rule's "only."
violations.fix_hint: Reconcile r6 and x7 at the Sheet level before implementing delegated rate change.

violations.where: R-d2 "An Invoice's `amount` equals the sum of its Line Item `amount` values" vs Invoice derived `amount` = `subtotal` − `discount_amount`
violations.why: R-d2 asserts amount is the plain sum of line items, but the Invoice model subtracts a whole-invoice discount. When a discount exists the two definitions disagree.
violations.fix_hint: Restate R-d2 as amount = subtotal − discount_amount.

omissions.why: Permissions note 2 cites ⟨src: n:n11⟩ which does not exist in the Sheet noun list (n1–n6); dangling/incorrect trace marker.

Sheet decisions d:auto_reminder_schedule (two automatic nudges) and d:late_fee_basis (flat late fee) are contradicted by the spec's manual-only reminders and no-late-fee stance; they conflict with d:overdue_reminders/d:late_fees but the spec never explicitly resolves the contradiction.

contradictions: Invoice status set vs. lifecycle: the data-model enum is `enum(draft,sent,partially_paid,paid,overdue,void)` with no `viewed`, but the Invoice lifecycle declares 'moves through 7 states' including 'viewed — Client has received/opened the invoice' and a `sent`→`viewed` transition. The two sections disagree on the legal state set (flagged by the compile report and still present).

Client permissions vs. viewed transition: the matrix Client column is all ✗ with note 2 'The Client holds no account and performs no in-app action' and non-goals 'there is no email open-tracking or "viewed" signal', yet the lifecycle row `sent`→`viewed` | Who: Client | 'Client receives and opens the invoice' makes the Client drive a transition using a signal the spec says does not exist.

R-r3 vs R-r7 / status derivation: R-r3 caps payments at 'amount minus already-applied Payment amounts minus applied credit-note amounts', so once any credit note is applied payments can never reach `amount`, making R-r7's `paid` unreachable; and status derivation defines `sent` only when 'credited_amount = 0', so a $450 invoice with a $200 credit and $0 paid matches no status — a permanently stuck, statusless record (per S22 it is 'settled-by-credit-note', which is not a status the enum defines).

Invoice amount formula: the data model derives `amount` = `subtotal` − `discount_amount`, but R-d2 states 'An Invoice's amount equals the sum of its Line Item amount values.' When `discount_amount` > 0 these two definitions of `amount` disagree.

Net terms location: the data model says `due_date` = `issue_date` + `net_terms_days` where `net_terms_days` lives on Firm Settings only, but S13 and Journey B step 5 say 'its due date is set by the client's net payment terms' — the Client entity has no net-terms field, so the per-client terms referenced in the scenarios do not exist.

Credit-note numbering: the Credit Note entity and R-d11 state credit notes use 'their own CN- sequence… kept separate from invoice_number', but the decision ledger entry d:credit_note_numbering answers 'They share the invoice number sequence.' The build source contradicts the decision it cites.

Deletion vs retention: d:deletion answers 'Records are never deleted, only voided/cancelled' (and R-r12 enforces it), while d:retention answers 'Until someone deletes it.' The ledger contradicts itself on whether deletion exists.

Reminders: non-goals and d:overdue_reminders say reminders are manual with 'no scheduled reminders', but the ledger also contains d:auto_reminder_schedule = 'Two gentle nudges: a few days before and after the due date' and d:auto_reminder_schedule is referenced nowhere to disable it — the two reminder decisions conflict.
Late fees: d:late_fees answers 'No' while d:late_fee_basis answers 'A flat amount added once' — contradictory ledger entries for the same feature.
unbuildable_requirements: The settled-by-credit-note condition (S22, status derivation) is described as an outcome but is not a value in the Invoice `status` enum, so a builder cannot store or query it.

'Attach or download files on an Invoice' is ✓ in the matrix and d:attachments = 'Yes', but the Invoice entity defines no attachment field(s), file size/type limits, or storage — a builder cannot implement it without inventing the schema.

'Undo the last field edit' (R-d8, S37) requires a prior-value history, but no entity stores previous field values or an edit log; the audit fields are who/when only, so undo is not implementable as specified.
'Send an overdue reminder' is a permitted action but no Reminder entity, template, or record of reminders sent is defined — the builder must guess whether reminders are logged.
`net_terms_days` is stated as firm-level with 'default 15' but scenarios reference per-client terms; the builder cannot tell whether net terms are one firm-wide value or per-client without guessing.

Idempotency for 'Send' is asserted (R-d5, d:x2) using an `idempotency_key` that only exists on the Payment entity; there is no send-idempotency key field or dedup window defined, so duplicate-send suppression is unspecified.
issue_date is 'set when sent' yet billing-day roll-off (R-d4/S9) sets 'the invoice date' at creation; the builder cannot tell which date field the billing_day drives or when it is assigned.
missing_for_a_builder: A single authoritative Invoice state set and the exact derivation for every state including any credit-settled state — this is the central unresolved question.
Whether discounts are in scope at all (d:invoice_discounts is 48% confidence) and, if so, the authoritative `amount` formula reconciled between the data model and R-d2.
The Client entity's payment-terms field (or explicit statement that terms are firm-wide) so due_date derivation is unambiguous.
Schema for invoice file attachments (fields, limits, permissions) given the matrix grants the action.
An edit-history/undo storage model, since undo and audit are promised but only who/when audit fields are defined.
A Reminder record/template definition and whether reminder sends are logged.
Resolution of the contradictory ledger decisions (reminders manual vs. scheduled; late fees yes/no; retention vs. never-delete; credit-note numbering shared vs. separate) before any code is written.
judgement.strongest_aspect: The rules-and-verification section (R-r1…R-d15) is unusually concrete, pairing each invariant with an executable verification sketch and specific dollar examples, which would make most individual rules directly testable once the underlying contradictions are removed.
judgement.weakest_aspect: Core money/state logic is internally inconsistent: the interaction of credit notes, the `paid`/`sent` derivations, and the R-r3 balance cap produces invoices that can reach a legal-but-undefined state and get stuck, which is exactly the kind of defect that corrupts financial records.
judgement.one_change_with_most_impact: Define one authoritative Invoice state model that explicitly accounts for credit notes (e.g., add a `settled`/`written_off` terminal state or make `paid` mean balance_due==0 with a separate payment-received flag), then propagate that single definition through the enum, status-derivation, lifecycle, permissions, and R-r7 — this resolves the three high-severity flagged contradictions and the stuck-record defect at once.
